title: Quantum Yang-Mills existence with a mass gap

concept.text: A mathematically rigorous construction of quantum Yang-Mills theory on four-dimensional space-time for any compact simple gauge group, proving a positive mass gap. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Quantum Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
page.definition: An interacting quantum theory of pure Yang–Mills fields, without matter, exists mathematically in four-dimensional space-time for every compact simple gauge group, which specifies its internal symmetry. A mass gap separates the vacuum from every excitation by a strictly positive energy.

goal.need: Pure SU(3) Yang–Mills theory isolates the gluon fields of the strong interaction. Six main lattice simulations with spatial spacings of 0.1–0.4 fm yielded a lightest scalar glueball energy of 1730 ± 50 ± 80 MeV, using an externally assigned physical scale. The uncertainties concern the lattice determination and scale setting. A construction and mass-gap proof would give this predicted spectrum a continuum mathematical foundation.

statements.quote: Quantum Yang-Mills theory is now the foundation of most of elementary particle theory

statements.body: Clay Mathematics Institute, Board of Directors
statements.quote: with $1 million allocated to the solution of each problem.
statements.context: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems announced on 24 May 2000.

completion.title: Yang–Mills theory exists on R⁴ with a positive mass gap for every compact simple gauge group.
completion.criterion: For every compact simple gauge group G, construct nontrivial pure quantum Yang–Mills theory on R⁴ with axioms at least as strong as the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader formulations, the prescribed local gauge-invariant observables and short-distance asymptotics. Prove that the Hamiltonian H, with vacuum energy zero, has no spectrum in (0,Δ) for some Δ > 0, and that m = inf(spec(H)∖{0}) is finite.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §4.
completion.basis: This is CMI’s mathematical target, including its requirements on observables and short-distance behavior. CMI currently lists the combined existence-and-gap problem as unsolved.

milestones.title: Four-dimensional lattice Yang–Mills theory has a self-adjoint, strictly positive transfer matrix.
milestones.criterion: At fixed lattice spacing a > 0 and finite spatial volume, construct the operator T that advances Euclidean time, with T self-adjoint and ⟨ψ,Tψ⟩ > 0 for nonzero ψ. This defines H = −a⁻¹ log T. Lüscher’s 1977 paper establishes this regulated result for SU(N).
milestones.set_by: Constructive quantum field theory’s physical-positivity criterion; Lüscher (1977), for SU(N).
milestones.threshold_quote: physical positivity holds in Wilson's lattice gauge theories

milestones.title: Four-dimensional Yang–Mills correlation functions exist with the ultraviolet cutoff removed.
milestones.criterion: Construct Euclidean correlation functions after removing the short-distance regulator while retaining a fixed infrared regulator. Magnen, Rivasseau and Sénéor’s 1993 result treats pure SU(2), the trivial topological sector and a regularized axial gauge; it checks infinitesimal gauge invariance through Slavnov identities.
milestones.set_by: Constructive quantum field theory’s cutoff-removal test; Magnen, Rivasseau and Sénéor (1993), for SU(2) under the stated restrictions.
milestones.threshold_quote: with a fixed infrared cutoff but no ultraviolet cutoff, in a regularized axial gauge.

milestones.title: Continuum quantum Yang–Mills theory is constructed on a compact four-dimensional space-time.
milestones.criterion: Give a complete continuum construction on a four-dimensional torus T⁴, with its field-theory properties established. On 9 November 2026, the Yang–Mills Shepherding Committee announced validation of a submitted Lean existence proof. That announcement is not peer reviewed and does not specify a finite-volume mass-gap bound.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §6.5.

milestones.title: Continuum finite-volume Yang–Mills theories have a positive mass gap uniform in volume.
milestones.criterion: For continuum finite-volume Yang–Mills approximations, prove one lower bound Δ > 0 on excitation energies above the vacuum that remains valid as the volume tends to infinity.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §§5–6.5.

not_found: The linked 10 November 2026 validation assessment could not be read; the committee’s 9 November 2026 announcement was accessible.

results.finding: Claimed continuum Yang–Mills hierarchy for closed matrix subgroups with nonabelian simple real Lie algebra; no sample size applies.
results.detail: The source claims continuum limits and field-theory properties, but does not specify a complete construction on T⁴. Its stated construction includes a volume limit, and a positive mass gap is outside its scope.
results.quote: Separated test-function moments have the full mesh limit at suitable fixed volumes, then the asserted volume limit.
